- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical lows after initial spikes.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimate as the horizon extends.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks, especially in the last 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent high values — overreacting to recent spikes, leading to overestimation.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 2–5% for the last 5–10 days of the 30-day horizon to align with observed mean reversion.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values in the first 10 days — apply a downward correction of 1–3% for early forecast days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — use a 10-day moving average or smoothed historical mean as a baseline for adjustment.
